_comment: sui's `builtins` registry, PINNED — the drift gate for the builtin surface.
WHY. sui's registry is a strict SUPERSET of CppNix's, and nothing noticed.
Measured 2026-08-17 against nix 2.31.5: the sui-eval tree-walker exposes
126 names to nix's 118, with ZERO absent — containment in exactly the wrong
direction. The consequence is a correctness defect with a very quiet
signature: an expression using one of the extra names MUST fail on real nix
(`error: attribute 'filterAttrs' missing`) and SUCCEEDS on sui. That is not
a missing feature — it is sui accepting a program nix rejects, which is the
one direction a compatibility layer must never drift in. Found by
`diff_filter_attrs`, which had been gated off behind SUI_TEST_ONLINE and
therefore never ran.
★ AND THE REGISTRY IS NOT ONE REGISTRY. Measured the same day, by this
gate's own first red run: `sui eval --json -E 'builtins.attrNames builtins'`
returns 124 names, and it is NOT the walker's 126. The difference is
BIDIRECTIONAL, so neither is a superset of the other:
in the walker, absent from the CLI (6):
builtins, flakeRefToString, parseFlakeRef, path, resolveFlakeRef, sui
in the CLI, absent from the walker (4):
fetchClosure, isStorePath, outputOf, toInt
`builtins.path` and the `builtins.builtins` self-reference exist for a
library consumer and NOT for anyone typing `sui eval`. Two evaluators, two
languages, one binary name. This is the same shape as the four disjoint
path-redirect namespaces already recorded in this repo, and it is the more
serious half of what this file documents — a superset is a permissiveness
bug, but a split registry means the answer depends on which door you came
through.
The CLI half is NOT gated here, deliberately: it lives in the bytecode VM's
builtin surface, which is under active change. Pinning it from this test
would fight that work. `pending-builtin-registry: gate the VM registry and
prove walker == VM`.
THE THREE CLASSES ARE NOT THE SAME DEFECT, and the split was measured with
`--extra-experimental-features`, not assumed:
experimental — a REAL CppNix builtin, merely gated behind an experimental
feature flag. `builtins ? fetchClosure` is false on a default nix and
true with `fetch-closure` enabled. Exposing one unconditionally is a
feature-gating divergence, not an invented builtin. Low severity. Empty
for the walker — both instances (fetchClosure, outputOf) are CLI-side.
nixpkgs_lib_leak — NOT a language builtin at any feature level. These are
nixpkgs `lib` functions (lib.filterAttrs, lib.strings.hasPrefix, …) that
were implemented into `builtins` instead of left to nixpkgs. Every one
verified absent from nix with ALL experimental features enabled. This is
the real defect class: six names, and any nix program using them is one
sui accepts and nix rejects.
sui_extension — deliberate, sui-specific, and namespaced as such
(`builtins.sui`, `builtins.resolveFlakeRef`). Divergence by design, not
by accident. Kept as its own class so a future leak cannot be filed here
to make the leak count go down.
THE OTHER DIRECTION IS EMPTY for the walker — zero nix builtins are missing
from it, which is why the superset framing is exact. (The CLI is a different
story; see the split above, where `path` is genuinely absent.)
HOW THIS GATE WORKS. The offline half always runs and is total: sui's live
registry must equal `sui_registry` exactly, so ADDING or REMOVING any
builtin is red until this file moves in the same commit. The online half
(SUI_TEST_ONLINE=1) additionally re-derives the classification against the
host's nix, so a name silently changing class is caught too.
NOT YET FIXED, and deliberately so: removing the six leaked names is a
behavioural change whose consumers span sui-eval/src/eval.rs and
sui-bytecode/src/{vm,builtins}.rs. This gate pins the current state and
makes the drift visible in both directions; the removal is the named
destination, not this commit. `pending-builtin-registry: drop the 6 leaks`
Gate: tests/builtin_registry.rs.
Partitions the walker's 8 names that real nix does not have. Verified
with --extra-experimental-features so `experimental` and
`nixpkgs_lib_leak` are separated by measurement, not by guess.
`experimental` is empty for the WALKER (the two feature-gated builtins,
fetchClosure and outputOf, exist only on the CLI side) — it is kept as
a declared, empty arm so a newly-added feature-gated builtin has an
obvious home rather than being mislabelled a leak.
Measured, not gated — see the header. The VM builtin surface is under
active change; this records the split so it is not rediscovered.
